sections.title: Library Membership Registration
sections.context: A student is talking to a library assistant about registering for a library card and learning about the facilities.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Good morning! Welcome to the Central Library. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Hi there. I'm a first-year student and I’d like to register for a library membership card. I was told I need one to access the digital archives.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: That’s correct. You’ll need it for the physical books and the online databases. Let’s get your details down. Can I have your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: It’s Maya Goldberg. That’s G-O-L-D-B-E-R-G.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Got it. And your student identification number?

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Let me see... it’s 99210... oh, wait, sorry! I'm looking at my old gym locker code. My actual student ID is 99201.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: No problem, 99201. And which department are you in?

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: I’m studying in the Faculty of Social Sciences, specifically the Psychology department.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Excellent. Now, for undergraduates, we have two membership tiers: Bronze and Silver. Bronze is free but limited. The Silver tier allows you to borrow more items and use the inter-library loan service. Most students go for Silver.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: I think I'll need the extra resources, so let's go with Silver.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Perfect. I’ll process that now. You can come back to collect the physical card on Thursday. We usually have them ready by Wednesday afternoon, but Thursday is safer.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Thursday sounds good. While I'm here, could you explain some of the rules? How long can I keep the books for?

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: For the Silver membership, the standard loan period for most books is 14 days. You can renew them online up to three times if no one else has reserved them.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And what happens if I’m late returning them? Is there a fine?

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Yes, we do have a late fee. It’s 2.50 pounds per day for each overdue item, so it can add up quite quickly.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: I’ll make sure to be on time! What about the study areas? I prefer working in total silence.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: In that case, you should head to the Third floor. The ground and first floors are for group work and can get a bit noisy, but the entire top floor is a designated quiet zone.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: That’s perfect. Do you have any scanners available?

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: Yes, we have high-speed scanners. Those are located in the Basement, right next to the computer lab. They are free to use, but you need to bring your own USB drive.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: One last thing—is there somewhere I can grab a coffee? I usually spend long hours studying.

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: We don’t allow drinks in the stacks, but we have a lovely cafe called The Atrium on the ground floor. It has a great selection of snacks too.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: The Atrium. Great, I'll check it out. Thanks for all your help!

transcript.speaker: Mr. Henderson
transcript.text: You're very welcome. Enjoy your studies!
